The Skellige Isles

Sailors give Ard Hugtand, also known as the Isle of Death, wide berth - and not without reason. Treacherous currents have cast many ships against its rocky shores, and hungry beasts inhabit the island and the surrounding waters. Though the isle’s inlets tempt them with their vast shoals of cod and salmon, even the most experienced fishermen do not dare sail near it. There are legends as numerous as they are varied, telling both of ravines filled with gold nuggets and hurricanes which whip icy, bone-rending shards across its surface. An absolute ruler has reputedly lorded over the isle for centuries, tolerating no intruders. These legends, however, remain only that, for no one who has ever ventured to Ard Hugtand has returned to deny or confirm them.

Kaer Trolde is the main fortress on the isle of Ard Skellig. For centuries it has been the an Craites' seat and jarl Crach an Craite’s pride and joy. Partly carved from the solid rock of the isle’s highest mountain, it makes a strong impression on all who behold it. Legend has it it was built by Grymmdjarr Iron Fang, son of Hemdall and Heulyn, founders of Clan an Craite. Grymmdjarr wanted a way to watch over all of Skellige to ensure no harm would come to his brothers, rulers of the other islands. So he wrapped heavy chains around a mountain resting on the sea floor, pulled it to the surface and placed it on the island of Ard Skellig. In seven days he carved out of it an impregnable fortress whose lofty towers afford a view of all the archipelago.

Vedymins, known also as witchers - a mysterious and elite caste of warriors cum priests. According to folk beliefs, they possessed magical powers and superhuman abilities, which they then used to fight evil spirits, monsters and other malevolent powers.
--Encyclopaedia Maxima Mundi, vol. XV

I know witchers just a bit less thoroughly then poetry and the fair sex -- meaning, I know them very well. During one of my many adventures, I befriended not just the famed Geralt of Rivia, but also his teacher, Vesemir, as well as his confreres, Lambert and Eskel. But enough about me.

In a nutshell, witchers are monster slayers for hire. They fight beasts with a silver-plated sword and simple spells known as Signs. The witchers' excellence in swordfighting is the result of years of excruciating training and magically induced mutations which greatly enhance their senses and reflexes. Unfortunately, these mutations, achieved through a rite called the Trial of the Grasses, are extremely dangerous and more often than not end in a long and painful death.

As a result of many provocations and slanderous gossip, witchers became first feared and then hated, leading in turn to persecution and pogroms which very nearly put an end to their caste. Yet some of them survived and ply their peculiar trade to this day, traveling back and forth across the Northern Realms, killing monsters for a small fee.

While riding through the village nestled at the base of Kaer Trolde, Geralt spotted a notice posted by a certain Odhen of Rannvaig promising a bounty for information about his missing son. It seemed like a job for a witcher, and since Geralt was, as usual, hard up for coin, he decided to look into it.

As Geralt passed through the village of Rannvaig, a man by the name of Odhen stopped him and asked for help in finding his missing son. The witcher, hearing honest fatherly despair in the man's voice and, no less importantly, feeling the lightness of his own purse, decided to look into the matter.
Geralt tracked down and killed the fiend - avenging the death of Odhen's son and making sure no more Skelligers would share the boy's fate.

Shortly after landing on Skellige's shores, Geralt was summoned by his old friend, Jarl Crach an Craite. The winded messenger who brought him this news did not know why his master had requested the witcher’s presence. Geralt, however, knew Crach well enough to know that the Jarl would not ask him to come without an important reason, and so he set off without delay towards Kaer Trolde castle, the ancestral home of the an Craite clan.

Geralt's first clue? A brutally murdered and mangled body. The villagers all agreed the Woodland Spirit had killed the man - but their explanations of this creature's motives could not have been more different. The elders among them claimed the Spirit, who had cared for their village for generations, was now punishing them for having broken the pact they had once made. As for the youth present, they claimed the Woodland Spirit was nothing but a cruel brute that killed for its own pleasure - and that rather than worship it, they should get rid of it once and for all.

Geralt promised to help with their problem - though he did not yet know which side was right. The witcher exercised his better judgment and decided his first move must be to find out what this Woodland Spirit really was - and why it had begun to kill.

No one is born a mage. We still know too little about genetics and the mechanisms of heredity. We devote too little time and resources to this research. Sadly, we still conduct trials in the inheritance of magic ability using, let us say, natural methods. The results of these pseudo-experiments far too often can be seen in the gutters of our cities and begging outside our temple walls. Far too often we see and encounter brain-dead and moronic women, women covered in their own spittle and passing themselves as prophetesses, seers, village diviners and miracle workers – cretins with brains degenerated by the uncontrolled Power they inherited.

These simpletons and fools can themselves breed, can pass on their “abilities” and continue the degeneration. Is anyone capable of foreseeing or defining what the last link in such a chain will look like?

Most of us mages lose the ability to procreate as a result of changes and disruptions to the functioning of our pituitary glands. Others – sorceresses, most often – mature into their magic powers with gonads intact. They can conceive and give birth – and have the audacity to consider that good fortune, a blessing. Yet I repeat: no one is born a mage. And no one should be! Aware of the gravity of what I write, I provide an answer to the question posed at the Summit in Cidaris. The cataclysm commonly known as the Conjunction of the Spheres happened one and a half millennia ago. A cosmic collision of several parallel universes, this disaster left numerous creatures not native to our reality trapped here. For example, ghouls and graveirs, which lack their own ecological niches, are simply relics of the Conjunction.

The elves claim that humans also arrived in this world during the Conjunction. This occurred soon after they managed to destroy their own world. The elves claim that it was during the Conjunction that humans learned to use magic.

Of course, these are all vile lies and foul fabrications circulated by nonhumans, who will resort to the most malicious slander to justify their claims.

To follow the example of the sorcerer from the tower, we first need to classify substances, diving them into superior and inferior varieties. Only the former can be described by the theory of interdependence presented here.

Inferior substances do not produce a chain of quasi-life structures, for their nature is substandard in quality and they cannot exist independently. However, it has been proven that they are paradoxically essential for the chain to exist in spite of their inferiority. The hypothesis of interdependence assumes that the chain of quasi-life must contain one substance of each superior element. Nonetheless, the chain's structure, proposed by Raffard the White, has one too few paces for them, namely only five. If the chain were transposed and then transmuted, the problem would easily be solved. Alas, the first operation cannot be performed without damage to the chain's integrity. The only solution is to use a so-called reversed transmutation, which will eventually cause the chain to rotate. As a result of rotation all six superior substances will constantly leave and join the chain without destroying it. From the holistic point of view, there will always be six superior substances occupying five places. The ingenuity of this solution lies in the chain having all the qualities of the three inferior substances. Thus the paradox of interdependence, or as some say coexistence, is no longer a problem.

Unfortunately, since none of the modern works describe how to perform reverse transmutation, the problem of animating the inanimate remains unresolved.

I'm supposed to find your family, and I will. With your dead baby's help.
May be something left of the one who got hit by the spell.
Wonder if he keeps an extra prick in his trousers, too.
You fuckin' deaf?
Go away. Or I'll kill you.
Dammit. Enough!
Seen this man before.
Inn at the Crossroads. You bought us a round.
As I recall, you were to go your separate way.
Baron home?
Depends who's askin'.
If he makes any trouble… well, we outnumber 'im.
Sergeant!
Talk to baron at Crow's Perch.
I'm too late. My only leads - the baron, and some witch.
Baron home?
Not your concern.
Need to talk to him. Open the gate.
Aye, her. That's right: I, a woman, am captain - shockin' as shit, I know.
Ever been there?
Farewell.
Ever sailed there?
Listen - the islanders attack all ships. When they hate someone - Nilfgaard, for instance - they attack 'em more, but truth be told not much more.
Boarded me once. Expect they wanted to see if I had captain's bollocks. That spot o' fun gave me enough Skellige for a lifetime.
Look for the ship's captain at the Golden Sturgeon.
Why help me?
Just looking to make some coin, or is there another reason you're helping me?
What you did at the Crossroads - that's why they won't let you in, right?
The innkeep? My sister's husband.
Years back, when the old lord still ruled Crow's Perch, the blacksmith's boy went missing.
Whole village looked for him. No luck. Finally found the boy in the river - he'd drowned.
Tragic. But how's that supposed to help me?
A few days on, an old woman who served the lord found the boy's cap near the castle well.
Well? Ready?
Clever man. Village folk built a shrine where they found the lad's body. Northwest of here. Wager you'll find an entrance to a passage nearby…
Hm, lit up like a charm.
What was that inscription again?

Four guardians, four flames, standing proud in a line. The First to light his fire dared not march on the end.

column7: Talk to Yennefer.
For one who never sees her, you seem to know a heap about her.
I know what they say. Don't care much meself, but when folk talk, I listen.
Oh, how we danced! How we twirled! Hahaha!
Attended a few, me and my Annie!
Twerked his back so bad last week he could hardly move. So I sent him to the witch. Came back sprightly as a foal!
Ooh!
One, two, three - one, two, three - wayhey!
We've not had a witch, shaman, nor cunnin' wench in ages.
I don't care how you do it, but the deliveries must be weekly.
Don't worry. Won't do your witch any harm.
Witch hunters been here?
No need to worry. I'm not out to hurt your witch.
Witch hunters've been here already?
Nay, but we've heard tell of 'em.
In spite of all that blabberin' about how cultured the nation is…
It's just that - blabber.
Didn't come here to chat.
Rumors rarely find confirmation in reality - especially the ones about foreigners.
I'm…
I know who you are. Believe I also know why you've come.
We'll talk inside.
Heheh. Right you are.
That it does.
When I learned you'd slaughtered my men, I thought to have you captured and hanged. Or at least flogged.
I'm no thug for hire.
But then I thought - one tough cocker if he bested that lot of cutthroats. Man like him could prove useful…
Useful for what?
I'm not a thug for hire.
I know who you are.
But since you come here having perpetrated that bloodbath, I assume you've something important to discuss.
I do.
Very well, then let's discuss it.
Useful? How?
That's the spirit! We'll work well together - I can see that already.
This way.
Not sure you're ready. You can barely stand.
Ah. Anchors aweigh!
I know who you are. Truth be told, it's the only reason we're talking.
I said already - I know who you are. Truth be told, it's the only reason we're talking.
How do you like it here in Velen?
It's awful.
Lovely place.
Get to the point.
I don't.
Lovely place.
Didn't come here to talk about the scenery.
You're wrong to avoid the topic. You've just arrived, plain to see. And the local swamps and bogs - they're interesting to say the least.
Someone loses their way 'round here, he becomes damn hard to find.
What're you getting at?
Oo, a weight off me heart, sir. She only arrived a short while ago, but she's frightfully wise.
Even pleasant on the eyes, if you like 'em skinny.
So when I spied ye comin', swords and all, straightaway I thought tales must be true.
I'm a witcher. Not a witch hunter.
Swamps, bogs, marshes everywhere…
Exactly.
Thanks for your help. Farewell.
Many have lost loved ones here. Some their wives, others their daughters…
Get to the point already.
Ciri. That's why you've come, isn't it?
So she was here.
She showed up some time ago - exhausted, wounded, and stinkin' like a soaked hound after a hard hunt.
Later I learned she'd come from the swamp…
That a threat?
What's that supposed to mean? That a threat?
Oi, not as clever as I suspected you'd be.
No, it's no threat. I'll spell it out for you - I know who you're looking for.
What now?
Now we pay a visit to Ermion's laboratory.
Didn't know we'd been invited.
Remember, you owe me. Butchered some of my better men.
Bloody elves. They'd invent any excuse to rob me.
Please, take this - a sign of my gratitude.
Heheh, sharp you are.
I regret your loss, commiserate. But you see, it so happens my wife and daughter are missing as well.
I understand. But you see, it so happens my wife and daughter are missing as well.
She's not from here.
You're up to something, Geralt. If I'm to help you, you must tell me what's going on. Who are you looking for?
Ciri.
Ciri? Well… now I understand the secrecy, not to mention the brooding, the furled brow. And you say she had some sort of problem with a witch?
So you haven't seen her.
I'm certain I haven't. But recently someone asked me about an ashen-haired woman. He claimed she would stand out from the peasant crowd.
Originally? Rivia.
Thanks, been a big help.
Who did the asking?
What else did he say?
Who was it?
He say anything else about her?
Not so fast, Geralt. No humble plea? No offering for the witch?
White Cat
Can we talk?
What about?
Nice to be together again.
See you.
Nice to be together again, wouldn't you say?
Mhm. Just missing Ciri.
See you later.
Yeah, take care.
Leif
Stranger in a Strange Land
Will ye forgive me?
Already have.
Fanatic
Preacher
Slave
Ardal!
Where is Ardal?!
A book? You mean to patch a henhouse?
My grandad once returned from his travels with a book. Fetched enough to buy him a home.
Stop chattering and help me search!
Greetings.
What is it? Hm?

Saying a botchling's ugly is like saying shit's not particularly tasty: can't say it's a lie, but it doesn't exactly convey the whole truth, either.
– Lambert, witcher of the Wolf School

Botchlings are perhaps the most repulsive creatures a witcher will ever have the displeasure of meeting. Born of dead, unwanted babies discarded without a proper burial, their appearance is that of a partially-decayed fetus, their unformed flesh twisted with hate, fear and malice. These hideous creatures feed on the blood of pregnant women, driven by a mad hunger that most often leads to their victim's death.
Let's go, then.
Yes, let's.
Botchlings
Read the bestiary to learn more about botchlings.
And luxury…
Don't mind him. Sit with us.
You're most welcome to. Though be warned - we're in the middle of some serious studyin', as our learned companion calls it.
Glad to join you.
Some other time.
Turns out I have something to drink.
Thanks. Be happy to join you.
What do they call you?
Kind of you to let me join you. And it just so happens I've got something to warm us up.
Well! The kind of guest I like! I shall find some mugs.
Day full of surprises, truly.
You saved us - we'd just drained our last bottle. What do they call you?
Look for a way out of the ruins.
Geralt.
Name's not important.
Love to sit down, but got a long road ahead.
War and death all around. You might take time to enjoy life a bit, seize the moment.
It's no wonder we're losing this war. Behold - a paragon of the Northern army seizing moments instead of fighting the Black Ones.
I'll leave you to it. Cheers.
I'm Geralt of Rivia. I'm a witcher.
I'm no one special. Fellow traveler, that's all.
Ah, our dear druid's laboratory. We must search it thoroughly. The Mask of Uroboros must be here.
Skelligers' tales about the Wild Hunt…
Letter bearing Ermion's seal… To the druids. Warns them about you.
Tales of the Wild Hunt

(…) The island folk of Skellige, like many nations of the North, hold a series of beliefs about the Wild Hunt as recorded in legends, myths and fables. This horrifying phenomenon is said to herald the coming of war and misfortune. Characteristic of their tales, and distinguishing them from their continental versions, is that the islanders imagine the Wild Hunt not as a cavalcade of wraiths galloping across the night sky, but as a ghostly longship. The vessel, called the Naglfar, is said to be built of "the claws of dead men." For this very reason, superstitious Skelligers remove the nails of their dead, expressly to prevent them from being used to fortify this ghastly ship. In many legends the Naglfar sails out of Morhogg - the land of chaos (…)
Ermion's correspondence

Brother druids,

Be forewarned that a sorceress has arrived on Ard Skellig. Her name is Yennefer and she hails from Vengerberg. I know you are immune to feminine wiles and will not let a well-draped skirt muddle your reasoning. Nevertheless, I warn you not to be taken in by her intelligence and refinement. I know who Yennefer is – I do not, however, know the true goal of her stay in Skellige. I see no point in asking her this question directly, for Yennefer is known for her cunning and eloquence. She says not what she thinks, but what she wishes you to hear. You must remember this is no second-rate sorceress. This is a person who breaks bread with the rulers of the North and who most recently has been working with the Nilfgaardian emperor himself. Familiar with courts the world over, she possesses an ability to manipulate that even the wiliest diplomat would envy.

Yennefer has displayed an unhealthy interest in the site of the cataclysm we are striving to study. I have not given her permission to go near it, but I caution you to keep your eyes and ears open all the same. The sorceress from Vengerberg is a stubborn and effective manipulator. I know that in the past her and Crach’s paths crossed. I suspect that she will wish to use this old friendship for some ulterior purpose. What that is, exactly… I will try to determine. Once I do, I will inform you in a separate letter.

May the Power be with you, Brothers
Ermion
A goat carved out of linden wood. Signed: "To Uncle Ermion."
Ermion's wand. He's one of the few druids to use one.
I have spoken to her, got my ways… So be it. You helped me, and I'm no boor. Come with me.
That old hag don't speak to strangers. And you're a stranger.
Exactly. Hm - Geralt… Heard that name before. You frequent the fairs?

You've confused him with Gerard, the stage artist who, indeed, attends fairs and breaks wind to the tune of popular melodies. To the delight of the crowds, I'd add. Our guest is none other than the White Wolf himself.
Well, my apologies. Ain't you the one that… you know, the rumors about Foltest's death…
No. Wasn't me.
Oh.
What's new in the world these days?
About time I left.
Any news? Of the war, for instance?
They say the Black Ones'll mount a new offensive soon, to cross the Pontar. I bet diamonds to peanuts Radovid won't manage to repel this time.
Such a shame Henselt perished in Lormark. Blasted Dragonslayer.
Let's try it. Think it's a nobleman…
You know a lot for an ordinary merchant.
I do. What of it? Hm?
Hands off the merchant.
Calm down, both of you.
Shame Henselt perished in the battle for Lormark. Now there was a king! He'd have rebuffed the Black Ones.
Time I was on my way. Thanks for your hospitality.
Leave him alone.
Relax. A misunderstanding, that's all this is.
Hah! Not a chance!
A Nilfgaardian spy in league with Foltest's murderer?
Stay a while. Road's no hare, it won't run off.
If he's in a rush, let him go.
Be on your guard. It could be something far more dangerous.
Heu-geh! No! Coral, nooo! I-I can explain everything! Akh akh akh…
Coral?
I never looked at the lass… you are my one and only!
Oooh… You're not Coral. Some succubus, a delusion… Where am I?
Right you are. With Henselt alive, Nilfgaard wouldn't 'ave had it so easy in the east.
Fine thing, that, sittin' down with folk and not introducin' yourself. Maybe you have something to hide?
Not this again. If he doesn't want to, then he needn't talk.
Indeed, it's rather suspicious…
Mighty suspicious. Best introduce yourself, mate - we don't like spies.
Geralt. I'm a witcher.
Think I should go.
Hah! Told you - a spy.
Damn, maybe he is.
I'll not let a spy walk free! To arms, gentlemen!
Shit.
Don't wanna cause any trouble. Farewell to you.
Truce! Truce! Lay down your arms!
He's dead.
You should go.
Dog's bollocks, I didn't want to kill him.
Mighta thought of that beforehand.
Aaargh…
Let's search his body. Might've been carryin' documents, a message.
You're on your own.
Thanks for your help - one Nilfgaardian spy less.
Rosa
We wish to come to an agreement, do we not?
Cregennan
Nilfgaardian Officer
Blood! We need blood. A living being.
There shall be no Forefathers' Eve this year… but we'll find a way, all the same.
You mention Forefathers' Eve?
I hear you right? You mention Forefathers' Eve?
Pretty old custom. Thought it had died out.
Light the tallow candles to lead them through the dark, call them by name, appease their regrets - only then may they depart in peace.
Death lurks in every bog and puddle 'round here. Folk know they could die, their earthly matters unresolved.
Then they require help, or they'll not know peace. Forefathers' Eve must be performed.
Greetings, Yen.
Razed huts and fresh graves. Hm, this must be it.
Gathering of some kind… We've come at a bad time.
There's no good time to talk about the Wild Hunt.
Damn… Dead… has been for a while.
Shit…
Fine, scrape together what you can and haul the bits up here!
Putrefaction's set in… but the vocal cords are intact. We might still get something out of him…
Talk to Yennefer in private.
Go to Ermion's workshop.
Find the Mask of Uroboros in Ermion's workshop.
Explore the secret chamber using your Witcher Senses.
What've you learned?
Transit passes at terrific prices.
Interest you in a pass? Cheapest around, right here.
How much for a pass?
Not interested.
Gotta think it over. So long.
I'll pay for the pass.
Maybe there's another way to do this…
I'll think it over, bye.
Sure hope the pass is worth this much coin.
You've made the right decision. Won't regret it.
Refused to help him.
This girl is in trouble.
Always better with a discount.
I'll think it over, bye.
Aye. Good idea. Discount's yours, my friend.
In that case, I'll take it.
I'll think it over, bye.
You live here alone?
Anyone else here? Besides you?
Whew, at last. But it was worth it, right? You learned something about Ciri in the end, something important.
Because we've not been.
Let's go.
We shouldn't.
Take it Ermion won't be there?
That's right.
And what's the purpose of this visit?
We're looking for an object - the Mask of Uroboros. We'll need it.
We shouldn't be breaking into Ermion's workshop.
If I didn't know you better I'd say you needed to grow a pair. But I know that you simply enjoy complaining - it's the only reason you said that.
Do you intend to venture into Crookback Bog? You must tell me about it afterwards.
Don't know that I'll get the chance.
Geralt, there are two types of men: those who see opportunity and take advantage, and those who forge the opportunities themselves.
I've always seen you as an example of the latter. Besides, I've a favor to ask you. So, visit me some time?
Be sure to stop by.
I'll try.
I'll stop by. You can be sure.
I'll try.
In that case, I shall be waiting.
See you, Keira.
Laboratory worthy of an imperial alchemist.
Refugee Leader
Simon
Gloria

The islanders believe the wraiths sail on a longship built of the claws of dead men.
…that brazen manipulator?
Thug
Little Ciri's handiwork. That's what she called him when he was her tutor.
Thug
Bandit
Ciri… Menge is following me… He has seized the treasure… He has Dandelion…
Footsteps… Not good.
A woodland spook?
No. And in general, don't venture too deep into the woods. You never know what a spook'll do.
Your boy now in the army, lost to you he serve us all.
Your boy now in the army, lost to you he serve us all.
Where's you goin'? That's a place o' culture, not a trough for swine to trudge to…
Yeah, I'll take one.
No. Don't want a ticket.
No. No need.
So be it. But you'll not get in. Whores through a window - them you can watch gratis. These here're artistes.
Yeah, one.
Here. Just stay outta sight, eh? Awful bashful, these mummers in rehearsal.
Door on the left.
Doesn't look like the talkative type.
Anyone can be made to talk, even a corpse… One must simply know how.
Need any ingredients for the spell?
Black magic's no joke.
Black magic's no joke. Casting those spells never ends well. Never.
I don't like it any more than you do, believe me. But the thought that Ciri is in danger? I like that even less.
I understand. Still doesn't give us the right to--
Geralt, please. This is not the time to debate ethics.
Need any ingredients for the spell?
Mhm. The blood of a newborn, a virgin's tongue and the eye of a newt.
Mind trying again, without the sarcasm?
I don't need a thing. I'm a sorceress, not a village herbalist.
All I need is energy… a great deal of energy. We're very lucky this place is saturated with magic.
It's also considered sacred. Priestesses'll be furious if you use the garden's Power to revive a corpse.
Geralt, you're getting on my nerves. I offer you solutions, you try to poke holes in them.
All the more reason to get it over with before they realize what's happening.
Watch it, tramp. Novigrad's not your stomping ground.
Ptooey!
What do ya want?
Got a problem?
Bloody hell!
Hit 'im! Kill 'im!
Son of a whore!
Together now! Kill the whoreson!
Hoo-wee at him!
Ploughing curses!
Try me, prick!
Argh…
Oof. That was close.
Have you any idea what could happen if it is used? Any idea of the consequences?
Shit!
Bravo! Jolly good stuff!
Bravo!
Bravo! Damned fine doppler! Looked real! Heheh!
Wolves!
Spooked Mare
Geralt met a man who claimed one of his horses had been stolen by some kind of woodland spook. The witcher promised to bring back the missing mare.
Find the missing horse using your Witcher Senses.
Quick! Hide!
Where is the holy garden?
Morkvarg? What's that?
Thanks for your help.
Defeat the Scoia'tael.
Thanks for your help.
Custom demands pilgrims make an offering of their own blood before the tree. Craven surely did so… Unless he lacked not only courage but respect for Freya as well.
Lead the horse into the enclosure.
Where is this holy garden?
Not far from here… North. We cultivated healing herbs there once…
And now?
You can come out now!
My, you're brave. My father couldn't even do that!
Heh. Mine could do a lot more.
Cor, could really use a piss, but about to get my arse wet.
You're carrion!
I'll rip your mug off, mutant!
Take him from the back!
This ain't doing shit!
Cover your eyes!
No, but neither do you. So stop panicking.
Eye for an eye!
Ploughin' hit the cunt!
Come on!
Worried this trail might've gone cold…
Even if Craven's dead… We'll manage.
How, exactly?
You'll see when the time comes.
This Morkvarg… half-man, half-wolf?
My thoughts are the shite.
And yet bother us he does.
Impossible. I split him open from head to…
You were not the first. Several brave lads have cleaved the beast… But Morkvarg always returns.
I know… Craven went there before you but has yet to return.
Didn't see him in the garden… Doesn't bode well. Don't know if there's much point in going there.
Hear that? Wolves.
Hide, quickly!
You didn't mention your heroic battle with this Morkvarg character…
You know me… Don't like to take my work home…
They're gone! You can come out!
You cut 'em up bad! The Wolf King will be angry.
Do parents often send their children out to follow the sweets?
Sometimes they send their children, sometimes they go themselves.
Look, there! Lindenvale!
Fine. Let's get to work.
Just thinking about the consequences.
Fine. Let's get to work.
Ivy-covered walls, a mysterious garden… Shame we're not here under different circumstances …
Thought you wanted to start at the tree?
Let's do what we came for and leave. Can't say I like this place.
We're about to make some enemies.
We are about to make some enemies…
I don't need everyone to like me. I most value the opinions of those I care about. You, for example.
Let's get to work.
Sorry to bother you with my doubts.
Please, Geralt…
So… can we start?
Mhm.
I'm not poking holes, just thinking about the consequences. How about you? Given them any thought?
I understand you intend to enter the garden?
I dislike it when foreigners enter the sacred grounds… But so be it.
Madame Irina? Can we talk?
Geralt of Rivia! Dandelion's told us so much about you!
So, where shall we start?
Plan to bleed yourself for the goddess?
Not necessarily. But Craven did… We just might pick up his scent.
No.
Geralt, I'll say it again… We're short on time. Ciri is short on time.
Mhm.
Fine, you busy yourself pouting. I'll handle the rest.
Which is why you should stay up here.
You can't help me track him… So I don't see any reason for you to go down there.
Control yourself, druid. I haven't stolen anything. I've merely borrowed something and fully intend to return it.
Hah! The generosity! Just one small problem - once used, the mask is rendered completely worthless!
Not to mention the risk you'll bury us alive! And all the Isles with us!
Argh, shove that poker up your arse.
Help me!
Uahahaha!
That's it! Yer in for it!
Slaughter the freak!
This way. Through the cave.
You lead.
Fuckin' come on!
Gotta get around 'im.
He's a warlock!
Bugger me mug!
It's a bit dark…
Afraid?
You stay here! I'll go and--!
I can look after myself.

What became of that creature? Where is he?!
Sssss-tooo-pp…. Hhh-urrrr-tsssss…
Begone.
Ttt-eelll… thhhh-emmm… Ccc-llleeearrrr… mmm-yyy… nnn-aaa….
Celain, celain, deffraen!
Celain, celain, davedar!

You died in battle. You've recovered your honor.
We're looking for Ciri. Ashen hair, green eyes… Have you seen her?

Take them in, give 'em a home. Won't steal from you, then.
Sure, but I'll be feedin' the whelps! I gain nothin' from it.
But… Suppose I'll give it some thought.
Keep watch - kids are likely to try again.
Oh, I'll be waitin' for 'em! With a stout branch to smack the little shits with!
Easy, they're just kids.
Aye, for now. But they'll grow into bandits, you wait!
Watch out… They'll be back.
Give 'em a home. Likely to stop stealing, then.
Found a group of kids in the woods. They were the ones stealing your hens.
Oh, children, eh? Ridin' on the backs of wolves, were they?
Never any wolves here. The kids are just… clever…
If they've anythin' in their noggins, they'll stay away from me hen house now!
I can help you. Not for free… But, you're advanced in years, so I won't ask too much.
Poppycock. "Not much," he says, but you'll take me liver come the end. Well, no one else's linin' up to help me…
Me hens started disappearin' about a week past. Always take one at a time, the vermin.
I can help you.
What happened, ma'am?
As if the war weren't enough, sir. I'm losin' me hens! How'm I to live? Eh?
Get a look at the thieves?
What thieves?! It's monsters takin' me chickens.
An ordinary thief I'd nab on me own, but beasts? What'm I to do?
Gonna gut you clean, you louse…
Aaaargh!
Now, left! Leeeft!

Greetings… Can we talk?
I found the thieves.
Farewell.
Take care, now.

Return to the old woman or give the children time to escape.
Ritual of some kind… We'll have to wait.
We'll do no such thing.

Can you not see we're commemorating the dead? So…
And we're looking for someone who's still alive. Please… This is urgent.
Ugh. Then speak.
We're looking for an ashen-haired young woman.
They say the Wild Hunt destroyed your village…
You're his friend - any idea where he might be hiding?

In the past, facing trouble, he'd disappear, then reappear on the morrow as someone else.
They say the Wild Hunt destroyed this village…
We're looking for a young woman, name of Ciri. Ashen hair, green eyes...
I'm sorry. She is not here.
Unless she lies in a grave… That is, I do not recall one by that name, but I've buried so many… I may have forgotten.
This… This Ciri… Has she a scar? Here, on her cheek?
But this time…? This time he hasn't returned.
We gotta convince Dudu to come out of hiding.

Don't know. Saw her but for a moment, right before… before it all. She was in the stables with… Craven.
Rainin' like hell.
{*Whistles*}
Can't bear to watch a man get his arse beat… just can't. Unless I'm doin' the beatin'.
Bloody easy!
Oughta land in the clink for an ugly mug like yours.
Oy!

Mummy!
Ow do.
Shit your pants already, bigboy?!
Die, fool!
Bloody hell!
Dragonplougher!
You smell like dead meat, arsehole.
We need to convince Dudu to reveal himself. Any friends we could leave a message with, someone he trusts…?
That is true… Though few believe us. You don't either, I'm sure.
Keep it together, lads!

Priscilla, actually. She's done writing it. Tells the story of a witcher who rescues a doppler from certain death.
Hm, sounds interesting. I'll gladly have a glance, but first we must think about getting the word out and organizing some protection - ushers.
Would you mind tending to these matters?
Why the ushers?
How do I help you publicize the staging?
Priscilla's done writing. I have her manuscript.
Thanks. See you.
Think we need ushers? A play about dopplers could be controversial… but are ushers absolutely necessary?
Can't be sure if you've attended many performances, but Novigrad crowds can be particularly… difficult.
Rotten apples, tomatoes, eggs - that sort of thing?
Axes, butchers' knives and bricks, actually.
All right… Know anyone appropriate?
Try the docks, perhaps. You're bound to find some men willing to do any work for a few crowns.
How can I help you spread the word about the premiere?
Well, we'd like all the city to hear about it, so we must clearly talk to the Puffins.
Who're the Puffins?
Street artists. Get them to announce the premiere and even the mussels on the harbor piling will hear about it.
Where'll I find them?
They did occupy some rooms in the Bits, in a townhouse, but I can't be sure they're still there. I've not seen them in the streets lately. They may very well have hung up their body hose…
See if I can find them, and if they'll work for us.
Thanks for your help. Be back with some ushers, and once Priscilla's done with the play.
See you then.
Priscilla.
Phew, I'm relieved. Time is short, but she's written many an excellent scene, practically in her lap, just hours before we've opened.
What will the play be about?
Not sure yet, but we definitely have to mention dopplers.
Hm, that could be risky. But… We must think about getting the word out - about the new play - and arrange for some ushers to keep the peace. Will you tend to that?
Dandelion's in trouble.
That much I guessed - though I am curious how serious it is.
Did he seduce a powerful man's wife and go into hiding? Or did he write an offensive couplet about the priests of the Eternal Fire?
Worse. Lots. I'm gonna try to help him. Gotta contact Dudu first.
But he's disappeared as well.
Have a plan to lure him out of hiding, but I need your help. Can I count on you?
Naturally, but what can we possibly do…?
How can I help? We've not seen Dandelion or Dudu recently…
Madame Irina?
In the flesh. And you must be Geralt, the White Wolf! Dandelion's said so much about you!
Is he with you?
No, but I hope to bring him back soon. Here to talk about Dudu.
What'll you do to me, eh? Eh? Eh?
Burdock - godlings hate the scent. How would you like a whiff?
Bleugh akh… Take this stupid 'ouse, you burdockin' bully!
Come by from time to time and ask. The de Jonkheers never break their word once given.
Shut up for a moment and look at me.
Think what you will, but I'll not stay in this bloody swamp one day more. Not one day!
I shall cross the Pontar, and that means Radovid's men will find me sooner or later. Don't you understand?! I don't have a choice. I will have to parley.
What the devil is a godling?
Post-Conjunction creature. Likes making mischief.
Your burdock. Will that do?
That's plenty, thanks.
Gain entry to Ernst van Hoorn's warehouse.
See the wake's in full swing.
Lost sight o' youse. Who won?
Actually, glad you're still here. Wanted to ask you about someone.
See you at Kaer Morhen?
Before I go… The notes, I'll take 'em.
So, see you at Kaer Morhen? Beds free of bedbugs… mostly.
I long to be there already… See you, Geralt.
Cerys, proving she's her brother Hjalmar's equal in every way. She retrieved the axe from the cliff.
Cannot be!
I lost.
Lost to a witcher, Sparrowhawk. That'd likely happen to any of us.
Meaning?
Her da's a Nilfgaardian aristocrat with the imperial legation. Commissioned Dandelion to tutor Rosa and her sister in the art of rhetoric, but wee Rosa preferred swordplay.
Where're those crafting supplies?
We're here. From this spot you must reach the top of that mount.
At the summit you'll see the stump of an oak, Hjalmar's axe buried in it. Whoever pulls the axe from the stump first, wins.
I'm ready.
You'll start when I sound the horn.
Show the little wench her place!
No cheatin' now!
Shall we put some coin on it, Lugos? Actually, dogshite idea - you never pay up.
Hurry it up, old man!
Hurry, axe handle's rottin'!
Show me what you've got, monster slayer!
Woman's Ghost
What do you want with those papers?
One thing - watch where you step.
How come?
Jarl's not too fond of light. Makes it easy to trip.
Naturally, you suspect me of the worst. I don't deserve that. My intentions are pure - like a virgin's tears.
Alexander was studying the Catriona plague. I'll use his notes to produce medication, perhaps a cure… or at least a vaccine.
Why, I aim to use them to continue important work that a man's tragic death put on hold.
Yeah, kinda… So before I go, I'll need you to hand me those notes.
All right, all right. Take them already.
Farewell, Geralt. Or rather, see you soon.
White Wolf!
Bah, tell Crach to calm down. No Skellige lass can perish in her own isles.
What ails you?
See you.
Means war's a-brewin'. Time to sharpen our swords.
With Bran dead, who will lead you?
Don't need a king to stick it to the Black Ones. No reason to wait.
You're back, White Hair.
You're not going anywhere. I carried you out of there a moment ago, half dead.
I have to--
Word is some mages died.
You have to tell me what's going on.
You're weak yet. You must rest.
Don't be daft. Cleaver weren't born yesterday. War's on. Bugger kips down somewhere new every night.
Hmph. Whoreson's in for it now. Cleaver's spiteful - won't let it slide.
Whoreson gets ploughed up the arse, we'll be next, you know.
We had peace, peace was good. Who found it a fuckin' bother?
Start! May the best man win!
Come now, don't cry. After all, he's not the only man in the world…
But he's a baronet! Where will I find another baronet?
Tell me a story about one of these weapons.
This sword's hilt is made of meteorite steel.
No, it's made from the heart of a falling star.
Whoever wields this sword will always find his way at sea, no matter how stormy the skies.
But after a time it overwhelms its owner with sadness and longin' for its starry home. And nothin', not even good fun and good company, can cheer him up.
Tell me a story about one of your weapons.
See this sword? You know by its crafter's mark that it was forged in the isles. Belonged to Lars, who woulda been the same age as I.
What happened to him?
His wife went missin' durin' a nasty storm. It was said the goddess smiled fondly on her, so Lars refused to believe she was truly dead.
He ran out on the rocks and begged Freya to give his wife back. Left his sword behind to show the gods humility. And never returned for it.
Selling that same sword now?
We coulda tossed it in the sea, but fish got no use for blades. He had no family, so I'm sellin' it… to the right man.
Battle axe looks pretty old.
Even older than this keep, and yet still sharp.
Once each year, at Saovine, this axe speaks.
It tells of blood spilt in battles, of burnin' villages and sunken boats.
Might be a curse, and might be it drank too much human blood. What's certain is no one wants it.
Beat Cerys to the top of the mountain.
Good reason to fight.
Lemme guess.
What else would Skellige boys fight about?
Whaddaya think - who'll be the next king of the Isles?
Hjalmar, clear as day. Lad's brave and generous, and from Crach's own line. No better claimant.
Let me guess. The sword was supposed to go to the first-born, but their father decided it would be the younger brother's?
But what we didn't and couldn't agree is that there'd be a war, now, could we?! My custom's been cut in four!
Quite a coincidence that's what I aim to do to you.
As custom has it, the clan sword should go to the firstborn son - Udalryk. But his father gave Brokvar to his little brother - Aki.
You know our customs well.
Well enough to know Udalryk probably considered that a serious insult.
Huh, serious insult in these lands.
Serious enough for Udalryk to break a sacred law here in Skellige - he openly questioned his father's decision.
Haha! Look at the redhead!
Go on, chase her! When a woman runs it means she wishes to be caught, desperately!
Close enough.
Can you make master-quality armor?
Looking for someone who can make me a master-quality breastplate.
Hm. Never known a master who wasn't a dwarf.
Fergus, perhaps? Say he's holed up somewhere in Velen.
Keep outta this, grayhead. Not your concern.
They make friends?
Something happened on that trip.
A storm broke out and Aki fell overboard. Udalryk had his hands full with the sails. Didn't hear his brother until it was too late.
Didn't hear… or didn't want to hear…
Some folk on the isle had the same doubt, but none would mention it aloud.
Most likely their father thought some hard work at sea together would fix things between them…
We use sea outings as cures for many things… Sadly, this time it didn't work.
Got a feeling this trip didn't end happily…
Your feeling's right. There was an accident.
Yeah… Four men. Collecting tribute from one washerwoman. Don't think I have much to fear.
Don't care. I don't believe it's the gods talkin'. Have you seen him? He's covered in scars.
Come on… Gold's gold.
I've asked around, here and there, visited our druids on Ard Skellig and Freya's priestesses on Hindarsfjall. And I've talked to Hjort.
But you have heard what Bedlam does to people who cross him? Or you need a demonstration?
What've you learned?
What do you know about Hjort?
C'mon, Fritz… Boss wants it that way, it's how it's gotta be.
This Hjort… Who is he, exactly?
A druid. Been servin' the Brokvar clan since Agnar, Udalryk's granddad, was jarl.
Da says he's the only reasonable man in the whole clan.
Open up, in the name of the Fire! There's a mage inside, we know it - one Remi Villeroy! Sentenced to death in absentia!
We've been courteous enough. Batter down the door, we're going in!
I think we've to give Brokvar to Aki, and he'll leave Udalryk alone.
Not a bad idea - on condition it's a ghost we're dealing with. But something doesn't add up…
What's that?
Aki drowned at sea - said so yourself. But the ghost haunts this house.
Aki and Udalryk both lived here. Maybe that's why.
Thanks for your help, Geralt, but I've gotta get the sword.
I won, but only by a hair.
No such thing. There's winnin', and there's losin'. And I lost.
Let's.
I'm first! Behold - Hjalmar's axe. I beat the famous White Wolf.
Congratulations.
Let's go back.
Be glad to tell everyone about your victory.
Crach could be right. Seems Hjort gave you a good lead.
I take it your suspicions were confirmed.
Thank you, oh thank you! To think there're men who'll help a stranger outta the kindness of their hearts…
Priestesses and druids wouldn't say much. But they agreed there's not much in the holy tomes about the gods commandin' folk to hurt themselves.
Morkvarg? Behind this wall, sounds like.
Hjort was the one really got me thinkin'. He told me Udalryk started hearin' voices right after Aki's death. Hjort thought that important.
Hjort has doubts as well?
Think it might be Aki's ghost?
So Hjort also doubts Udalryk's been chosen by the gods.
He's loyal to the clan, so he'd never say openly. But he suggested that Udalryk's troubles likely come from Aki.
Hmm… So you think it might be Aki's ghost, not the gods?
Besides, now we've got the sword, we'll soon see if that's what it's about.
Hmm, no harm in trying, I suppose.
Forgive him, Jarl. Geralt's got more to learn about our customs.
We're close to the gods in Skellige. And the chummier y'are are, the greater the offerin' you make.
And that's where little witchers come from.
That's it?
I'm not sure what you're getting at, but I should make one thing clear - men don't interest me. Told him that as well.
Besides, men don't interest me. I told him that from the start.
That why you think I should look for my friend there?
I meant no offense.
It's our belief the greatest thing a man can offer is his pain, his suffering - the pure sacrifice.
Jarl, the witcher surely meant no offense. Let us hear what he has to say.
Not entirely outta kindness, and you're not entirely a stranger.
What're you…? Oh, I know you! You're that witcher took Dandelion out whorin'… Jerald, right?
Covered in blood - all of it! So much work, for naught.
No need to thank me. It was nothing.
Sorry… Don't get me wrong, I'm grateful, but… Everything I had… I just lost.
That the gods are angry at you, yet he's the reason. That's why you have to apologize - to Aki himself.
Relax… It'll come out in the wash.
Course it will. Just gotta soak it in white vinegar - but that's not my point.
Junior shan't forgive me. Either I close up shop meself, or he'll burn me down.
Remi Villeroy. You are under arrest for sorcery and conspiracy. Take him.
Daddy!
Vesemir'd say, "Stay out of it"… But Vesemir's not here.
The gods won't be pleased.
Explain something, if you don't mind… You say I took Dandelion out whoring?
So he said. Claimed I was his one and only, but he fell in with the wrong folk - you and that dwarf who always looks like a cow licked him. Said you two were a bad example - wine, women…
Not Jerald… Geralt.
Oh… Dreadful sorry.
Sorry… Didn't think about that.
A woman's lot… Men have their fun, and we're stuck with the mess.
… song. He pick that habit up from us, too? Gotta have a word with him…
The gods are that cruel?
Don't be afraid.
Angry you want to make peace with your brother? Are the gods of Skellige that cruel?
I swear… you're worse than door-to-door peddlers.
Don't know if you remember - we've met.
I don't-- Wait, wait! I know you! You're that witcher I near clobbered with a vase when… Well…
They are that just.
Justice demands you return to the dead what is rightly theirs.
What would you have me do?
But that's a tale for another time.
Illnesses catch 'em at times - other times they wanna catch a bit o' diversion.
We have to return his sword.
Thanks for your trust.
You've made the right choice.
You shouldn't listen to everything people say about--
Uuhh…
When you kicked Dandelion out… through the balcony. Actually, he's the reason I'm here. Know where he is?
I believe so as well.
Stop… Hear that…? They've come for us.
The fool didn't break until I began to prick his heels.
Every man's got his sensitive spots. Interrogated a mage once, pain couldn't touch him. Tore off his fingernails, crushed his bollocks… Nothing.
We were lucky this time, but… you'd best leave via the sewers. The trap door's in the floor.
Take care of yourself, Kluhg.
I've never even intimated--
Look for crevices… And droppings…
Whaddaya think… Where could Dandelion be?
Probably out whorin', that hoarse pheasant, that lyin' scoundrel!
Ouch… What'd he do to get your goat?

Same thing as ever! Prize bullshitter came back, sayin' it was till death do we part this time. And? No more'n a week passed before I spotted him in Harborside, strollin' with some trollop on his arm!
Twas the last straw. All those questions 'bout the washerwomen at the bathhouse, then this. I beat 'im black and blue and threw 'im out on his ear!

Geralt learned of a witcher who had earned the ire of several villages in Velen. One of the inhabitants of Lindenvale had even accused him of fathering his daughter's child. The whole affair seemed highly suspicious, so Geralt decided to investigate and find out the truth of the matter.
Leave, witcher. Or I'll find some iron jewelry for you, too.
Ye strayed from the path, witcher. Means you lost.
Froze me arse off for nothin'. Fuck this, let's go warm up with some mead.
Help me! They'll burn me! Burn me alive! I've done nothing!

Nothing? Nothing?! Who concocted those poisonous potions? Who helped the Lodge of Sorceresses, sending them reports via megascope? Who addled men's minds with magic, eh?! I know you, Remi. I know you and your crimes.
Can't allow this.
Can't get involved.
When'd the gods speak to you? Right after I left?
Listen - when I find Dandelion… anything I should tell him?
Oh well… I suppose I must move to Oxenfurt. Professors need clean undergarments, too.
Shortly after. Sleep came over me, so I lay down. 'Twas then they revealed their will to me.
You always asleep when they speak to you?
There's an oneiromancer in town - Corinne Tilly. Very capable, supposedly.
Never trusted in dreamers' abilities myself.
Corinne's been very effective - you should at least try.
She's taken a job close by. Follow the canal, away from the fish market. The house is near the first bridge. Its owner, de Jonkheer, is a rich banker.
You know, I've been thinking… who might know something about Ciri. And I just got an idea.
Always.
What do you see then? Do they try to summon you anywhere specific?
Now get!
My old home. They command me to light torches, then speak from the shadows.
That was long past. It shan't happen again!
Oh, we'll make sure it don't. Shackle him. His cunt, too.
Can't allow this.
No one's asking your mind, mutant.
Collective responsibility, is that it? Not terribly fond of that strain of justice… But don't worry… won't get involved.
Good of you. See, witchers are like dogs - useful so long as they do what they're trained for. But when they start biting the wrong hands, no one hesitates to break their necks.
The gods don't like light?
Do they always demand an offering of pain?
Together I expect you'll resolve things twice as fast. You've the look of true experts.
Have you ever seen them?
The gods speak from the shadows, you said. Is that why you don't allow any lights in here?
In my dreams. Atimes I see their form. When the torches burn bright.
Dunno why ye strayed from the agreed path, witcher. But if one were to ask me, I might say ye gave up.
Be that as it may, still a good excuse for a drink. Crach's rolled out some prime mead!
To see the gods is a great honor. Maybe, with more light in your house, you'd see them when you're awake as well?
Lesser men are unworthy, they cannot gaze upon their faces.
The gods always demand you offer them your suffering?
Only that pleases them, so they ask for more and more.
Don't much like merchants who flatter with cheap praise before the job's done.
That was not cheap praise! I was merely stating a fact.
So am I.
But I'd prefer you not to tarry and begin.
All right, then… Let's get to work.
The gods ever show you their form? Or are they always just a shadow?
Once, I steeled myself, gathered my courage, and in my dream made my torch burn bright. I saw a hazy figure sitting in shadow then.
Bolted shut…
Mischief, you call it, yet it's likely to prevent me from selling.
I can try to smoke it out. I'll need burdock.
Did Corinne dream of the building's past?
Yeah… Pretty horrid, apparently, though she refused to talk about it. Nobody should inhabit the place.
Sit there. There, I said! And shut it!
All right, all right. But what then? How long do you think you can keep me in this hut?
Cerys, we need to talk.
Sorceresses - no greater pleasure to be had in interrogation. Love it.
Word is Menge's gonna issue an order - ban us from having our fun.
That's right… except it's the other way around. I'm always saving him.
Mean to say it weren't Dandelion saved you in Flotsam by severin' your noose with an arrow from a hundred paces?
Mhm. Wouldn't be here if not for Dandelion.
Told me all about your adventures. How he'd ready you for battle with his songs, how he tamed the kayran by playin' his lute…
Didn't need a recommendation. Name would've been enough.
Father always said: "All ought to know your merits, son. Don't hide them under a bushel."
I'm a Redanian countess one day, a dockside thug the next. That is true freedom!
By the Eternal Fire… I've never seen so many before.
Looks unsavory. What is all this?
The trappings of a black magic ritual. Witches weave human hair through dolls they first curse. They gain a grasp on individuals' souls this way.
Think one of the dolls represents Anna? Can we free her if we find it?
It's the only way I know of, but there are risks involved. The items woven into the dolls - see them?
Uhh… No, no, didn't see any.
The stallion danced betwixt her thighs! Lather bathed its chinny-chin-chin.
What? Dandelion couldn't… Er, never mind. Any idea where our master archer might be at the moment?
I meant that literally. Dandelion's why I'm here - came to ask you about him. Know where he might be?
No… sadly, I haven't got a clue. We've not seen each other in ages.
Turned out he was devilishly ticklish. I placed a beetle on his belly and set a mug atop it. Damn near went mad.
If Dandelion and I hadn't laid our cards on the table at the start, I might have suspected he had a history with the alchemist. He spoke like a lovesick beau.
In fact, he desperately wished to meet with him.
Why would he do that?
Says they're to suffer, whereas the cunts just dream of getting ploughed well and good.
Argh, he exaggerates. Besides, we do his dirty work and deserve a bloody reward, am I right?
Said there'd be strawberries and that wine with the bubbles, and he'd sing me arias… But… I've not seen him since.
Yes, yes, yes! Do that and I promise not to bother your friend. Not even a little. You're awfully nice, you know?
I don't hear that often. Thanks.
Thank you! If you hadn't intervened, they would have killed me. And Louisa, and the boy… I tremble at the thought.
Triss Merigold. Find her. Might be able to help you.
I hope so. Take this. I must abandon magic for good. You might still find use for it. Perhaps the next time you encounter mage hunters…
Yeah… Something tells me it won't be long… Farewell.
Where do ye want to go? Golden Sturgeon or the Seven Cats?
I'll not set foot in the Sturgeon. The scum they employ to serve patrons there--
Heheh. Admit it. You've eyes for that servin' wench at the Cats.
You're to return for rehearsal. Today, is that clear?
[Hand him Toradar's fang.]
Nooooo!
I'll kill ye… I'll kill all you whoresons!
Leave it! Or they'll cut ye down, too…
Keep your distance.
We want no trouble, move along.
The var Attres gave alms last week.
Piss off! None of your kind'll get in here on my watch!
Mhm. Different mothers, too.
Maybe… But you could see he cares for her, looks after her, the way he carried her packages and…
Know where I can find her - Dandelion's sister?
Can you show us how to cut off a head?!
Can we try your potions?
All right, arrange a meeting.
Want me to help you get supplies?
Not interested.
Sorry. Negotiations? Just not in my line of work.
Should you change your mind, you know where to find me.
Want me to help you get your supplies? How?
Just come with me to a meeting. As my bodyguard, it'll bolster my confidence. Truth be told, not so long ago I tried negotiating some iron deliveries with one of the King of Beggars' men.
Dammit. Who's this now?
Cleavers' boys!
They symbolize the individuals the dolls are meant to represent. We must find the doll that is Anna and take it from here.
Mentioned a risk…
How do you know all this?
This risk you mentioned - take it we only get one shot at choosing the right doll?
I'll not chance it. I did not know Anna… You've learned much of her. Should find it easier to choose.
All right. Let's take a look at these dolls.
Seem to know a lot about this.
Grab a wooden one. And take care not to hurt the little miss, or you'll earn the ambassador's ire.
From tomes on black magic. Initially, we burned any that we found. Recently we decided it might be wise to read them first.
Escape the ambush.
Poisoning your minds with magic, heh, superstition? What's the hierarch think of that?
Have you met the man?
No.
Neither have I.
Follow me.
… is Geralt of Rivia, I know. Dandelion's told me a great deal about you, and I've listened with bated breath.
Don't be surprised. After all, doubt I could think of a more fitting subject for a ballad than a witcher's love for a sorceress…
Morkvarg
… Sheep dip…
… And I've not seen him since.
Grab a wooden practice sword.
Or should I say - sorceresses?
Take it the heist was a bust?
Reuven? Who's that?
Breaking into a vault… what was Dandelion thinking?
Bards - not people I confide in.
Seems Dandelion left nothing out.
There's a good reason I don't pour my heart out to bards - they always babble, as you just demonstrated.
But listen, besides giving you the details of my affairs, did Dandelion mention his own plans, where he might be going?
Seems Dandelion was meticulous in telling my story, down to personal and insignificant details. Did he offer anything about himself - like where he was going?
Hahahahah! Splendid! Very funny, truly! So, see you later!
Not here. Come with me.
Wooden sword
Reuven… What's he like?
Dandelion breaking into a vault… I'd sooner expect him to choose a life of celibacy.
True… Forgot to pay for his wine at the Passiflora once. He laid awake the next three nights worryin' about it.
It feeds on their pain for years, fueling their guilty conscience. In the end, hyms force their victims to mutilate themselves.
Hrrrr you cannot hide your stench… hrrr mmmm... rrrrrefrrrreshing… hrrr hrrrr…
Can't hurt it otherwise.
I dare you to say it again!
Not enough he's a heretic, he's also a liar! What'll we do with 'im?
Any idea what got into him? He have debts he needed to pay off?
He claimed he was helping someone. An urgent matter that couldn't wait, he said.
This "someone" - Dandelion mention their name?
No… But if I know Dandelion, it's "her" name he failed to mention. As he failed to mention "her" slender waist and ample bosom.
Lemme guess - attempted heist was a failure?
Well he's not driven up in a gilded carriage laden with jewels, so I should think so.

I've asked after him everywhere, but it seems an army of tongue-stealing cats has overrun the city. I learned only that he raised a ruckus at Whoreson Junior's lair. Then Whoreson's men chased him all over town.
Tall… Fat… Dangerous as hell.
Limp in his gait - left leg.
Sounds like a lame rock troll.
If trolls were devilishly intelligent and had a flair for crime, yeah, I'd agree.
Whoreson Junior… Doesn't ring a bell.
Biggest prick in Novigrad. Not literally, but…
Got it. You're not a fan. But what'd he do to you?
Try the whole town. He's one of four bosses who control the city's underworld - the others being Sigi Reuven, Carlo "The Cleaver" Varese and the King of Beggars.
Looks like I gotta rescue Dandelion… again.
Hope Dandelion gets out of this alive…
Here I go again, rushing to Dandelion's rescue… He oughta pay me a salary.
Dammit… Hope Dandelion gets out of this alive…
And in one piece. Know what they do to bards? Break their fingers, or tear out their tongues… Or both.
How's here, tomorrow? Same time as today?
See you, master witcher.
Relax, I'll get him out of this. Gotta talk to this Whoreson first - and Sigi Reuven. Know where I might find them?
I don't know about Whoreson but Reuven runs a bathhouse. Careful, though… he's a dangerous character.
Wherever he is, I sincerely doubt he's in the mood for jokes. Nor am I, in fact.
So am I.
What's exciting about it?
Very. I'm looking for Dandelion.
Uh, what's so exciting about it?
I don't doubt it… but Dandelion's not. I beg you to hurry. Let me know as soon as you learn anything.

Duke de Wett led the Verden Group. To describe the manner in which he did so as “incompetent” would be far too kind. Facing a force half as strong as his own, he delayed the northern offensive, turning all his attention to the fight against the guerillas of Verden.

Something about life in dreary backwoods settlements leads their inhabitants to hide the truth with misleading names. This takes the form of both hyperbole - a clump of bare trees called "Dragon Spike Forest" or a hole in the ground two paces deep named "The Chasm of Eternity" - and understatement - a horrid massacre calmly referred to as "the incident." Velen fit the mold in this regard, as Geralt learned while he wandered through it in search of Ciri. There he encountered a trio of highly suspicious magical sisters called the Ladies of the Wood, who directed him to a clump of bogside huts known as Downwarren. Geralt was to solve their "problem": a rash of mysterious murders. He spoke to the ealdorman and learned that the evil power behind the killings dwelled in the Whispering Hillock. Wherever else?
