My Dear Friend,

If you're reading this, it means you've found the chest I mentioned in my previous letter. You'll be pleased to know its contents belong to you.

After I spoke with the emperor regarding additional resources to aid in your quest, he was willing to part with these items from his personal collection. The armor from Dol Blathanna is a rare piece that marries the strengths of Nilfgaardian and elven craftsmanship. Apparently, Francesca accepted Emhyr's offer of Nilfgaardian plate for her forces. Though, despite his attempt to significantly bolster an ally on the fringes of the Northern Realms, only a portion of his aid ever reached its destination. To no one's great surprise, the elves were unimpressed with what human steel they did receive and thus refashioned the armor to their liking. You'll finally have the opportunity to masquerade as the Queen of Dol Blathanna's personal guard. It's a dream I know you speak of often.

As for the second set of armor, the emperor proved far more cryptic. He claims they were diplomatic gifts from distant kingdoms. The tiger armor is specifically designed to suit a western ruler – obviously Emhyr in this case. It was forged in the ancient style of a blacksmith who stole the secrets of its construction from their gods... Or so the legend goes.

And finally, the swords (to my eye they resemble a Redanian saber, though I'm no expert). These blades supposedly once belonged to a hero of myth and mystery. The man forged a pact with a vixen spirit and, through her blessing, was granted the ability to slay the monsters that had long plagued his village. As you can see, he carried both a steel and silver sword – a fact I thought might pique your interest.

Unfortunately, legends are all I can offer. Emhyr was stingy with the details – even more so than usual. It's a shame because I must admit I haven't the faintest idea where they might originate. That being said, I do believe Zerrikania and Ofier can be ruled out.

Dear friend, I trust you appreciate my efforts to help. Use these gifts as you see fit. I hope they will hasten your search for that which we have lost.

Your friend, Yennefer

Last letter from Robert

Son,

I hope you’re well and this letter finds you. Please make sure your sister and her little sprouts know that I’m all right. The Black Ones’ attack didn’t prove as fierce as it must have appeared to you from the outside looking in, though that’s not to say they were altogether gentle. I was fortunate to flee a fortnight after Belleteyn. Still, before escape seemed possible, for the first time in my life, I sat haunted by the thought I may never see any of you again.

You know your old man is as tough and stubborn as they come, and I’m sure I’ll manage from here on just fine. But you and your sister are grown now – you know life can, and often will, turn us from the paths we set for ourselves.

I had hoped to reunite with you in Redania, but chances of that grow slimmer every day. These damned Nilfgaardian bureaucrats refuse to let anyone cross the border. I’ve already arranged to set out tomorrow for Aedirn with a band of dwarves. They claim to know of another route, safe and swift. Gods willing, perhaps I’ll even arrive first and welcome you myself. Yet, if fate does decide to lead me elsewhere, at least I shall have good company and a new adventure ahead of me. One unlike any other before.

I intended to keep this letter brief, so I shall end it here with only one request – should anything happen to me, do not let the world change you. Stay true to yourselves as the good folk you are and always take care of each other.

Until we meet in Rivia,

Your father, Robert S.

And so the time has come for me to die. Of starvation, in the dark, alone, in my own manor, while my servants bring in a fresh harvest just beyond these walls. My cries are in vain. No sound escapes from this stony grave, from the tomb that fiend Roderick sealed me in. Yet that is not the worst wrong he has done me. He stole my Dolores… and so I curse him, a thousand curses I call upon Roderick of Gors Velen! Not for taking my life, but for taking from me the one who gave my life meaning.

If anyone ever finds my remains and this letter, please, seek out my sister, Dolores Reardon, and tell her the truth – that I was killed by the man who seduced her, the man she left me for, the scoundrel Roderick of Gors Velen. He struck me from behind, dragged me here and then walled me in while I lay unconscious. He did not even have the courage to slit my throat.

Yet, despite it all… I hope he brings her happiness – if so, I will rest in peace… But if he fails her, my ghost will haunt him to the end of his miserable life, and he will die as I have – alone and forgotten.

Stop Horse - Motion Patterns
To stop your horse, turn each Joy-Con 2 inward.

Tilt each Joy-Con 2 slightly back, then slap them down to gain speed. Perform this multiple times to increase speed from a canter to a gallop.
